description.short_caption: Chest radiograph showing bilateral pulmonary opacities and medical devices.
description.detailed_description: This is an anteroposterior chest radiograph showing bilateral pulmonary opacities, more pronounced in the right lung, suggestive of consolidation or infiltrates. Medical devices, including ECG leads and a nasogastric tube, are visible. The cardiac silhouette appears enlarged, and there is evidence of a possible pleural effusion in the right lower lung field. The image is de-identified and includes standard radiographic markers.

Case_13011/figure2.jpg.source_caption: Radiograph of the chest, lateral view.

description.short_caption: Lateral chest radiograph showing lung fields and thoracic structures.
description.detailed_description: This is a lateral chest radiograph displaying the thoracic cavity. The lung fields are visible, with some areas of increased opacity in the lower lung zones, which may suggest consolidation or fluid accumulation. The diaphragm and heart borders are also visible. The bony structures, including the ribs and vertebrae, are well-defined. No obvious foreign bodies or gross abnormalities are noted.
visible_findings: lung fields with areas of increased opacity
bony structures including ribs and vertebrae

description.short_caption: Axial CT of the chest showing bilateral pulmonary infiltrates.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the chest demonstrates bilateral pulmonary infiltrates, predominantly in the right lung. There are areas of ground-glass opacities and consolidation, suggesting an infectious or inflammatory process. The mediastinum and heart are centrally located, and no obvious pleural effusion is visible. The image is in lung window settings, enhancing the visualization of parenchymal abnormalities.

Case_13011/figure5.jpg.source_caption: CT of the chest, one month after first admission.

description.short_caption: Chest CT showing bilateral pulmonary abnormalities one month after admission.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the chest demonstrates bilateral pulmonary abnormalities, including patchy areas of ground-glass opacities and consolidations. The findings are more prominent in the lower lung fields. There is no clear evidence of pleural effusion or significant mediastinal lymphadenopathy. The image is consistent with a follow-up study, likely assessing progression or resolution of an infectious or inflammatory process.

description.short_caption: Chest radiograph showing bilateral pulmonary opacities and medical devices.
description.detailed_description: This is a frontal chest radiograph showing bilateral pulmonary opacities, more prominent in the lower lung fields. There are medical devices visible, including a right-sided central venous catheter and a left-sided pacemaker or defibrillator. The heart appears enlarged, and there is evidence of possible pleural effusion or consolidation in the lower zones. The image quality is adequate for interpretation.
visible_findings: possible pleural effusion or consolidation in lower lung zones

Case_13011/figure6.jpg.source_caption: Figure 6. Blood culture growth, gram stain (400x magnification).

description.short_caption: Gram stain of blood culture showing filamentous structures, suggestive of fungal or bacterial growth.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a gram stain of a blood culture at 400x magnification. The central feature is a dense, tangled network of filamentous structures, which are darkly stained against a lighter background. These filaments suggest the presence of a filamentous organism, such as a fungus or actinomycete. The background contains scattered debris and lighter staining material, consistent with the culture medium.

Case_13011/figure7.jpg.source_caption: Blood culture growth, Hanks Acid Fast Stain.

description.short_caption: Hanks Acid Fast Stain of blood culture showing filamentous branching structures.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a stained preparation from a blood culture using Hanks Acid Fast Stain. The field reveals filamentous, branching structures stained blue against a purple background, consistent with acid-fast organisms. The morphology suggests the presence of filamentous bacteria or fungi. The background appears granular, likely representing cellular debris or other culture components.
